chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: I may be traveling, and the time for salat (prayer) arrives, and I fear the burning heat of the ground on my face; what should I do? He said: Perform sajdah on part of your garment. I said: Not every garment allows me to perform sajdah on its edge or hem. He said: Perform sajdah on the back of your hand, for it is one of the places of sajdah.

key_terms.تَسْجُدُ: you perform sajdah; the act of prostrating in salat (prayer)
key_terms.ثَوْبِكَ: your garment; clothing used here as a surface for sajdah
key_terms.ظَهْرِ كَفِّكَ: the back of your hand; an allowed place for sajdah in this circumstance
key_terms.ٱلرَّمْضَاءَ: the intensely heated ground or scorching earth
key_terms.ٱلسَّفَرِ: travel; the state of being away from home during which this ruling applies
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer); the obligatory ritual prayer whose time has entered
key_terms.ٱلْمَسَاجِدِ: places of sajdah; bodily parts or places associated with prostration

ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do for sajdah if the ground is too hot during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for sajdah during travel when the ground is so hot that it harms the face. It permits performing sajdah on part of one's garment, and if that is not possible, on the back of the hand, identifying it as one of the places of sajdah.
